description: Shapes 6 (mixed512 b640, ~164ms) and 7 (mixed1024 b60, ~108ms) sit on the cuSOLVER floor, but the 'mixed' generator builds a HETEROGENEOUS batch: _MIXED_WEIGHTS gives ~40% dense plus ~60% individually-cheaper structures (rankdef/nearrank 3n/4-rank, band bandwidth~16, repeated <=16 distinct eigenvalues, psd/spectrum/rowscale geometric-decay low-effective-rank, clustered 2-level). A prior naive gather-split lost (206 vs 164ms) because it ran two solvers serially and mishandled the non-low-rank structures. Build a per-matrix STRUCTURAL CLASSIFIER via cheap batched probes (off-band L1 energy for bandwidth, trace(A^2)/||A||^2 for effective rank, diagonal dominance, cluster/repeat detection) that routes each matrix in the batch to its fastest validated path -- the existing low-rank subspace solver for rank/geometric-deficient matrices, a narrow-band path for banded ones, the two-level projector for clustered, batched cuSOLVER only on the genuinely-dense remainder -- gathered by class and scattered back under the per-matrix residual gate. Adopt brief-8's banked 50x solve_triangular contiguity fix and robust cholesky_ex CQR2. Route only n in {512,1024} mixed batches; homogeneous batches keep their current paths (no regression).

t1: per-matrix mixed router (classify->2-level/low-rank/cuSOLVER)+brief-8 CQR2 contiguity fix. REGRESSION 43265->47008us. mixed512 router 223ms vs 163ms cuSOLVER: serial multi-solver trap (cluster=87 lowpr=122 rest=431; cuSOLVER on 431 rest ~130ms + low-rank floor + 2-level). cuSOLVER marginal rate ~267us/mat already excellent so removing <60% cannot beat it. Need floor-free path for 41% dense majority -> extend megakernel to n=512.

t3: cost-gated mixed router (predict route vs whole-cuSOLVER from class counts, route only if <0.80*whole; homogeneous->delegate to 2-level; consolidated single A@A; tightened 2-level detector 0.6->ncl=37). 44240us (parent 43265). Gate correctly falls both benchmark mixed shapes to whole cuSOLVER (no partition wins); residual ~2.3% regression = router A@A+syncs on mixed shapes + extra A@A on clustered512. DECISIVE BRACKET: no Python-level partition beats whole-batch cuSOLVER on mixed512/1024 (best 3-way 163.8==163.6ms; 147 vs 105ms). Lever is floor-free n=512 batched kernel (cluster megakernel verified compiles on B200).

t4 (clean no-regression): revert brief-8 CQR2 (MEASURED 0.96-0.98x SLOWER here -- k=352-768 dont hit the transposed-trsm pathology); enhance _eigh_twolevel SPLIT branch (only entered for >=50%-2-level clustered-heavy batches) to peel low-rank matrices (PR<50) to the floor-free low-rank path. Benchmark mixed shapes are <50% 2-level so hit the early whole-cuSOLVER return at EXACT parent cost -> 43289us == parent 43265 (0.05%, noise). clustered512 keeps 2-level win (66 vs 138ms). Dead router+pre-screen removed. Profiled mixed512 (gemvx/gemv2T-dominated = cuSOLVER syevd floor). BRACKET: no Python-level partition beats cuSOLVER on mixed512/1024 (best 3-way 163.8==163.6ms; 147 vs 105ms). Lever = floor-free n=512 batched kernel (cluster megakernel verified compiles on B200).

Brief-10 (mixed per-matrix routing) worked out across 4 trials; HEAD=133f082b7 = parent-equivalent 43267-43289us (parent 43265, 0.05% noise), no regression, validated 39/39.

DECISIVE BRACKET of the brief's thesis: a Python-level gather/split router CANNOT beat whole-batch cuSOLVER on mixed512 (b640, 163ms) or mixed1024 (b60, 105ms). Evidence, all measured live:
 - cuSOLVER cost model: n=512 = 25ms floor + max(0,b-64)*0.24ms/mat; n=1024 = 61ms floor + max(0,b-28)*1.375ms/mat. The per-matrix MARGINAL rate is already excellent.
 - Per-class breakdown (mixed512): dense 264(41%), psd 76, rowscale 46, band 50, nearrank 45, repeated 50, spectrum 40, clustered 37, rankdef 32. Classes are cleanly separable by cheap probes (offband16_frac~0 for band; PR: rowscale~27, psd~42, dense~55, rankdef/nearrank~83, spectrum~111, repeated~286, clustered~512; A^2~cI for clustered).
 - Best-possible 3-way partition (dense->low-rank k352 + clustered->2-level + rest->cuSOLVER) measured 163.8ms == 163.6ms whole on mixed512, and 147ms vs 105ms (LOSS) on mixed1024. Even the MINIMAL router (clustered->2-level + rest->cuSOLVER) was exactly break-even (163.6ms). Root cause: removing any subset keeps cuSOLVER above its knee (>64 mat), so its cost drops ~linearly by the same amount the fast path adds; low-rank beats cuSOLVER on the DENSE majority by only ~10% (63 vs 68ms) -- too thin to overcome the classifier A@A (~4ms) + second-call overhead. Whole-batch cuSOLVER is a local optimum for these heterogeneous batches.
 - Whole-batch low-rank is dead (k=352->47% gate-fallback->220ms). Per-class low-rank split dead (each call carries a ~28-60ms floor; 9 classes = 9 floors).

TWO measured findings banked in HEAD: (1) brief-8's contiguous-RHS+cholesky_ex CQR2 fix is a 0.96-0.98x SLOWDOWN on THIS codebase (routed k=352-768 do NOT hit the transposed-trsm pathology brief-8 saw at (640,512,384)) -> reverted. (2) _eigh_twolevel's split branch (entered only for >=50%-2-level clustered-HEAVY batches, which the benchmark mixed shapes never enter) now also peels low-effective-rank matrices to the floor-free low-rank path -> live, self-gated, zero cost on the benchmark.

THE OPEN LEVER (unmeasured, warrants a dedicated brief): the ONLY floor-free path that beats cuSOLVER on the DENSE majority is the fused megakernel (measured n=448 b640 = 98ms = 1.36x, 153us/mat, NO batch floor). It caps at n<=448 because packed-FP16 lower-tri needs 262KB > 232KB SMEM cap at n=512. I VERIFIED thread-block clusters (compute_100a, cudaLaunchKernelEx cluster dims, cg::cluster_group + map_shared_rank DSMEM) COMPILE AND RUN correctly on this B200 with -O2 -- a 2-CTA cluster gives 2x232KB DSMEM, fitting a row-distributed n=512 packed-FP16 reduction (~128KB/CTA at a balanced row pivot). A cluster megakernel at n=512 would let the WHOLE mixed512 batch (and homogeneous dense512 shape 3, and the 208ms lapack_dense_even512 shape 11 -- off my brief but the single biggest shape) run floor-free at ~1.3-1.7x. RISK to measure: the distributed symv needs remote-DSMEM reads for the cross-block half of each matvec (higher latency) -- may erode the gain; must be built and measured, not reasoned. mixed1024 (n=1024=1MB packed) needs ~5 CTAs/cluster -- separate question.

OTHER OPEN DIRECTIONS not pursued: (a) the existing -O3 --use_fast_math on the megakernel module violates the run-wide -O2 constraint (latent large-batch nondeterminism risk) -- orthogonal cleanup. (b) a dedicated batched NARROW-BAND (bandwidth<=16) tridiagonalization for the band class -- but band is only 7.8% and cuSOLVER's per-matrix cost is structure-independent (~247-300us/mat), so peeling band alone won't beat the floor; only worth it fused into a floor-free kernel. (c) whether the low-rank peel in _eigh_twolevel helps at LARGER clustered-heavy batches (b>=400) where fixed floors amortize -- I only tested b=200 (0.96x, floor-dominated).
